content.heading: CatCheck helps you monitor, it does not diagnose
content.intro: CatCheck records the color of the indicator granules in the litter tray and tracks changes over time. What you see in the app is observational information for reference only — it is not a lab test result, not a medical diagnosis, and does not replace an examination or testing at a veterinary clinic.
points: Color can be affected by many factors other than your cat's health: room lighting, your phone camera, the shooting angle, food, water, medications, humidity, and how long the litter has been in contact with urine.

A single result doesn't say much. What matters is the trend — repeated changes compared with your own cat's usual level. When you see an unusual result, a common approach is to keep monitoring for another 24–48 hours, except in the emergencies listed below.

CatCheck doesn't know which cat just used the tray. If you have several cats, you need to pick the right profile before saving a result. If you're not sure, skip that entry — data assigned to the wrong cat is noisier than no data at all.
A result within the reference range doesn't mean your cat is completely healthy. Many health problems don't change the characteristics of urine.
content.outro: Every decision about your cat's health should be made together with a vet. Think of CatCheck as a monitoring journal to bring to vet visits, not something that answers in place of a vet.

phCard.title: pH reference range
phCard.body: {{catName}}'s scan results will be compared against this range.

step1.title: Fill a fresh litter tray
step1.body: Make sure it's at least 4cm deep so complete clumps can form.

step2.title: Wait for your cat to urinate
step2.body: Scan within 3–5 minutes after your cat goes, while the litter color is clearest.

step3.title: Open the CatCheck camera
step3.body: Line up the circle on the discolored litter; the system balances the lighting automatically before reading the color.

roadmap.title: Your next 3 steps
roadmap.intro: Start monitoring {{catName}} from the very next litter tray visit.

step1.title: Scan the litter color after your cat urinates
step1.body: Use the camera to scan the discolored litter in the tray within 1–2 minutes after your cat goes.

step2.title: See the color analysis & pH reading
step2.body: CatCheck balances the lighting automatically, estimates pH, then compares it against the reference range.

step3.title: Export a record to bring to vet visits
step3.body: Scan history is saved and can be exported to PDF for you to share with your vet.
